lens_description: Internationalization + Localization. Per ADR-0064 canonical-base + localization overlay. RTL support, CJK rendering, ICU MessageFormat + Fluent, per-pack overlay completeness, KR/JP/EU/KSA coverage.
subject: keystone-bundle-2026-05-20 (ADR-0242..ADR-0255, 14 foundational doctrine ADRs) + UX best practices + i18n canonical + per-pack overlays + user stories
corpus_examined: docs/standards/ux-best-practices.md (§5 Localization, §3 Accessibility, §2.3 Typography CJK fallback)
verdict_rationale: The i18n substrate (ADR-0206 Fluent + ICU MessageFormat), the canonical-base/pack-overlay model (ADR-0064), and the per-pack regulatory bundling (ADR-0251) together form a coherent, production-grade i18n + L10n architecture. The corpus demonstrates discipline that exceeds industry norms (Stripe, Linear, Microsoft Purview): single-source Fluent authoring across six native client stacks; ICU plural with locale-aware categories; RTL-by-default via logical CSS properties; CJK-aware typography (font fallback stack, +1px CJK minimum, +10% line-height, no italic/letter-spacing); pseudo-locale (xx-AC) in CI; per-pack composition (seam/adapter/pack trichotomy with ADR-0064 §1.5 semantic-localization decision rules). The reservations are gaps in the keystone bundle proper (ADR-0242..ADR-0255), not the i18n substrate: ADR-0251 does not bind compliance-pack agreement templates (BAA/DPA/SCC) to localized renderings, ADR-0240 sovereign-cloud overlays are silent on locale-data-residency mapping, and the keystone bundle does not enumerate per-locale ATO/regulator-facing language obligations (KR FSS Korean-language disclosure, KSA Arabic-language disclosure, JP Japanese-language disclosure, EU per-Member-State language). These are addressable in follow-on IPs; they do not block the keystone landing.

top_findings.title: Compliance-pack agreement templates (BAA/DPA/SCC) not bound to localized Fluent overlays
top_findings.rationale: ADR-0251 §D-7 declares agreement_template_refs (baa_template_ref, dpa_template_ref, scc_template_ref, subprocessor_disclosure_template_ref) as monolingual ref pointers. GDPR Article 12(1) requires data-subject-facing terms be in 'clear and plain language' — i.e., the data subject's language. KR-PIPA Article 22 likewise. JP APPI consent must be in Japanese for JP residents. ADR-0251 schema does not require per-locale variants of agreement templates. As written, a HIPAA-2024 BAA could ship English-only; a KR-PIPA DPA could ship English-only; neither would satisfy regulator scrutiny.
top_findings.impact: Regulator-facing audit could fail at first pack-install in non-English jurisdiction.
top_findings.recommendation: Amend ADR-0251 §D-1 agreement_template_refs schema to require a map of locale → template_ref instead of a single ref. Bind per-pack consent_grant_workflow_ref and consent_revoke_workflow_ref to locale routing. Add CI lane oya gate validate agreement-locale-coverage.

top_findings.title: Sovereign-cloud overlay (ADR-0240) silent on locale-data-residency mapping
top_findings.rationale: ADR-0240 §D-1 declares sovereign_data_classes (PII_KR, HEALTH_RECORD_KR_TIER1, GOV_DATA_KR) but does not bind these to locale-bound content authored in that jurisdiction. A KR tenant whose Fluent ko-KR overlay is generated and stored on AWS us-east-1 (CDN, build artifact, translation memory) violates the sovereign-data intent in spirit if the overlay carries PII-laden sample/test strings.
top_findings.impact: Translation-memory and Fluent-overlay supply chain becomes a sovereign-data leak vector; not enumerated as a controlled surface.
top_findings.recommendation: Cross-reference ADR-0240 in ADR-0206. Add §D-8 to ADR-0240: 'Per-pack Fluent overlays and translation-memory snapshots for sovereign packs must be authored, stored, and served from sovereign substrate.' Add catalog entry in registry/data-class/ for L10N_PII_<pack>.

top_findings.title: EU pack collapses 27 Member States + 24 official languages into single row
top_findings.rationale: INTERNATIONALIZATION.md §1 lists 'en-GB / en-EU' as a single locale row. EU GDPR rights notices must be served in the language(s) of the Member State of the data subject. With 24 official EU languages (BG/CS/DA/DE/EL/EN/ES/ET/FI/FR/GA/HR/HU/IT/LT/LV/MT/NL/PL/PT/RO/SK/SL/SV), the platform's tier-1 Western set covers DE/FR/IT/NL/ES — i.e., 5 of 24. Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Estonian, Finnish, Greek, Hungarian, Lithuanian, Latvian, Maltese, Polish, Portuguese-PT, Romanian, Slovak, Slovene, Swedish, Irish — all absent.
top_findings.impact: EU AI Act Annex III refusal banners, GDPR DSAR responses, and EU NIS2 incident notifications may be unservable in the data subject's language. Per-Member-State regulator (DPA) could reject the platform's compliance posture.
top_findings.recommendation: Add tier-2 EU locales to ADR-0206 + INTERNATIONALIZATION.md: pl-PL, sv-SE, da-DK, fi-FI, el-GR, cs-CZ, ro-RO, hu-HU, pt-PT minimum (top-9 by speaker count + regulatory weight). Extend pseudo-locale CI to surface drift for EU tier-2.

top_findings.title: ICU MessageFormat plural categories — no Arabic 'two/few/many' coverage test fixture
top_findings.rationale: i18n-canonical.md mandates ICU plural categories (zero/one/two/few/many/other) and ADR-0206 cites locale-driven plurals. Russian uses 4 forms; Arabic uses 6 (zero/one/two/few/many/other). No test fixture in the corpus enumerates Arabic plural correctness; pseudo-locale (xx-AC) only lengthens strings, doesn't exercise plural.
top_findings.impact: Arabic + Russian + Polish + Czech plural forms may regress silently; oya-check-i18n-coverage measures coverage in basis-points but does not validate plural correctness.
top_findings.recommendation: Extend oya-check-i18n-coverage with plural-category validation: per locale, every plural Fluent variant must enumerate the locale's required CLDR plural categories. Add test fixtures at clients/i18n/test-fixtures/plural-{ar,ru,pl,cs}.ftl.

top_findings.title: Hijri calendar dual-display (KSA/UAE) not in ICU formatter recipes
top_findings.rationale: INTERNATIONALIZATION.md §1 cites 'gregorian + Hijri + KSA holidays' for ar-SA. ux-best-practices.md §5.5 cites only Intl.DateTimeFormat with gregorian. KSA government-facing surfaces typically require Hijri date primary with Gregorian secondary, or both side-by-side. No formatter recipe enumerates Hijri (Islamic) calendar.
top_findings.impact: ar-SA/ar-AE surfaces may render Gregorian-only in regulator-facing or invoice contexts; FATOORA invoice may be technically valid but conventionally wrong.
top_findings.recommendation: Add ICU recipe to i18n-canonical.md for Islamic calendar (calendar: 'islamic-umalqura' for KSA, 'islamic' for general). Add JP era calendar (calendar: 'japanese') as parallel. Document dual-display pattern in ux-best-practices.md §5.5.

top_findings.title: Pseudo-locale (xx-AC) tests for length expansion but no pseudo-RTL or pseudo-CJK
top_findings.rationale: ux-best-practices §5.9 specifies xx-AC pseudo-locale (accents + 40% length expansion + bracket wrapping). No pseudo-RTL locale (e.g., xx-ZA Hebrew-mirror) and no pseudo-CJK (xx-CJ wide-character stress) are specified. RTL bugs hide until ar-SA snapshots run; CJK font-fallback bugs hide until ko-KR/ja-JP/zh-CN snapshots run.
top_findings.impact: RTL and CJK regressions land later and cost more.
top_findings.recommendation: Add pseudo-locales xx-RT (Hebrew-mirror RTL) and xx-CJ (CJK wide-char fallback) to clients/i18n/ tooling. Wire into CI snapshot lane.

top_findings.title: Keyboard shortcut localization gap (en-anchored mnemonics)
top_findings.rationale: ux-best-practices §8.5 acknowledges en-anchored mnemonics (c=Compose, j/k=navigation) and states 'do not localize the keybinding itself; tooltip text localizes.' This matches industry convention (Gmail, Slack, VS Code). However, the doc does not address: (a) keyboard layouts where the en-mnemonic key is in an awkward position (AZERTY for fr-FR, QWERTZ for de-DE, Korean Hangul layout, Arabic layout); (b) right-Alt = AltGr in many EU layouts collides with shortcut combos; (c) IME-active state (Korean/Japanese/Chinese) often intercepts single-key shortcuts.
top_findings.impact: Power-user productivity claim (no-code-first + power-user keyboard) degrades meaningfully outside en-US layout.
top_findings.recommendation: Add per-stack guidance for IME-active state handling (suppress single-key shortcuts while composition is open). Add fallback bindings (e.g., g h AND go-home-button) so layouts that can't reach j/k easily still have a path.

top_findings.title: es-US (US Hispanic) not differentiated from es-MX
top_findings.rationale: INTERNATIONALIZATION.md §1 lists es-MX for MX market but the US Hispanic locale (es-US, ~42M speakers, with currency-display + date-format + idiom divergence from es-MX) is not enumerated. tier-1 list per ADR-0206 cites es-MX + es-ES only.
top_findings.impact: Minor; most US-Hispanic users tolerate es-MX. Becomes a marketing/UX concern if oyatie targets US healthcare or finance B2C with Hispanic-segment focus.
top_findings.recommendation: Add es-US to tier-1 backlog with low priority; flag for review when US healthcare pack (FERPA/HIPAA US) graduates from planned to active.

top_findings.title: Indic script support not enumerated beyond hi-IN
top_findings.rationale: INTERNATIONALIZATION.md §1 lists 'hi-IN / en-IN' for IN-Mumbai. India has 22 scheduled languages (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, etc.). DPDPA 2023 requires consent language in the data subject's preferred language. Devanagari font fallback stack is not enumerated in §5.4 (which covers only CJK).
top_findings.impact: DPDPA tenant onboarding may fail in non-Hindi Indian markets.
top_findings.recommendation: Add Indic script section to ux-best-practices §5.4 covering Devanagari (Hindi/Marathi/Sanskrit), Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Gurmukhi (Punjabi), Gujarati font fallback. Add ta-IN, te-IN, bn-IN to tier-2 backlog.

top_findings.title: Coverage gate uses basis-points but no per-locale tier policy in keystone bundle
top_findings.rationale: i18n-canonical.md §coverage-gate states 9500 bps (95%) for production locales, 9000 bps (90%) tier-2, 8000 bps (80%) beta. The keystone bundle (ADR-0242..ADR-0255) does not bind these thresholds to compliance-pack readiness in ADR-0251 (e.g., a tenant installing HIPAA-2024 should require KR-PIPA-binding tenants to have ko-KR at 95%+ before the pack-install workflow completes).
top_findings.impact: Pack-install workflow could permit a tenant onboarding without locale prerequisite.
top_findings.recommendation: Add to ADR-0251 §D-3 step 'jurisdiction match' a sub-rule requiring locale coverage ≥ tier threshold for the pack's jurisdiction language(s) before stage 4 (DPIA signed) can proceed.

strengths: ADR-0206 unifies Fluent + ICU MessageFormat across six native client stacks (SvelteKit, Leptos, SwiftUI, Compose, GTK4, WinUI3) with one source of truth — exceeds Stripe/Linear cross-platform parity.
ux-best-practices §5.3 mandates logical CSS properties (padding-inline-start, margin-inline-end) and explicitly forbids padding-left/margin-right — RTL-by-default at the CSS level.
ux-best-practices §5.4 CJK rendering rules are unusually precise: +1px size, +10% line-height, native-region font primary in fallback stack, no italic, no letter-spacing.

ADR-0064 §1.5 semantic-localization decision rules (account classes via seam, FHIR via pack adapters, retention via seam, Cedar policy slots, etc.) is rigorous — handles ambiguous cases that most platforms punt.
ADR-0064 §8 canonical-base neutrality CI lane (regex Kr|Us|Eu|Jp|Sea|Mena|jurisdiction-codes) mechanically prevents jurisdiction leak into canonical base.
Pseudo-locale xx-AC in CI catches concatenation bugs before merge — industry-leading discipline.
ADR-0206 in-house roadmap correctly classifies Fluent + ICU as community/standards layer; no NIH rebuild.
Per-pack composition (manifest + corpus.lock + per-µservice overlays + Cedar fragments + Workflow templates + Typst templates + acceptance evidence) is comprehensive.
KR pack #1 fully specified down to identity providers (KakaoTalk/Naver/공동인증서) and payment rails (카카오페이/네이버페이/토스).
ADR-0251 §D-1 schema includes jurisdiction_overlay[] array enabling country-level + state-level overlay enumeration — extensible to per-language overlays with the schema amendment from F11-001.
